comparisons.peer_summary: Citi's short-term borrowings increased 29% year-over-year and 17% sequentially to $49 billion as of December 31, 2024, primarily driven by higher commercial paper issuances at broker-dealer subsidiaries as part of efforts to diversify its funding profile.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Citi report significant year-over-year increases in short-term borrowings driven by active management of liquidity and funding profiles. BAC notes a $11.3 billion increase primarily due to higher unsecured borrowings to manage liquidity needs, whereas Citi reports a 29% increase to $49 billion, driven by higher commercial paper issuances at broker-dealer subsidiaries to diversify its funding profile. Both disclosures highlight the use of short-term debt as an active tool for liquidity management rather than passive balance sheet growth.

sentences.text: Short-term borrowings increased $11.3 billion primarily due to higher unsecured borrowings to manage liquidity needs.

Citi's short-term borrowings of $49 billion as of December 31, 2024 increased 29% year-over-year, reflecting higher commercial paper issuances at the broker-dealer subsidiaries, as Citi continues to diversify its funding profile, and increased 17% sequentially, driven by the commercial paper issuances and normal business activity (see Note 19 for further information on Citigroup's and its affiliates' outstanding short-term borrowings).

comparisons.peer_summary: Unsecured short-term borrowings include long-term debt maturing within one year, hybrid instruments, and commercial paper used to finance liquid assets. Group Inc. does not issue short-term debt directly, other than to subsidiaries, in compliance with regulatory requirements.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies utilize unsecured short-term borrowings for liquidity and cash management. BAC identifies unsecured borrowings as the primary driver of its $11.3 billion increase in short-term debt. Similarly, Goldman Sachs uses unsecured short-term borrowings, including commercial paper, to finance liquid assets and for cash management purposes. Both disclose the composition of these liabilities involving commercial paper and other unsecured instruments, though BAC quantifies the volume change while GS describes the structural purpose and regulatory constraints (e.g., Group Inc. does not issue short-term debt directly).

sentences.text: Short-term borrowings provide an additional funding source and primarily consist of Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) short-term borrowings, notes payable and various other borrowings that generally have maturities of one year or less.
Short-term borrowings increased $11.3 billion primarily due to higher unsecured borrowings to manage liquidity needs.
A significant portion of our unsecured short-term borrowings was originally long-term debt that is scheduled to mature within one year of the reporting date.
We use unsecured short-term borrowings, including U.S. and non-U.S. hybrid financial instruments and commercial paper, to finance liquid assets and for other cash management purposes.

comparisons.peer_summary: Short-term borrowings increased, driven by Markets, reflecting net issuance of structured notes due to client demand, and higher financing requirements.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPMorgan report an increase in short-term borrowings, but they attribute the growth to different operational drivers. BAC attributes its $11.3 billion increase to general 'higher unsecured borrowings to manage liquidity needs.' In contrast, JPMorgan attributes its increase specifically to the Markets business segment, driven by 'net issuance of structured notes due to client demand' and higher financing requirements, indicating a client-flow-driven increase rather than solely a passive liquidity management action.

peer_results.rationale: Morgan Stanley's relevant disclosures focus on its strategy to reduce reliance on short-term credit-sensitive instruments by issuing borrowings with maturities greater than one year, and on total borrowings (including long-term) increase. This contrasts with the target topic which focuses specifically on the composition and increase of short-term borrowings (maturities <= 1 year) used for liquidity management. MS's disclosure explicitly states it issues borrowings > 1 year to reduce reliance on short-term instruments, making it not directly comparable to the specific short-term borrowing dynamics described by BAC.
